title: “I’d rather go to jail than getting beat up by my dad” Kaden (15)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 15-year-old Kaden. Kaden disclosed that his father was physically abusing him by punching him in the head. He also reported that he believed his father drugged him and his girlfriend and sexually assaulted Kaden’s girlfriend while Kaden was blacked out and incapacitated. When Kaden spoke to the CSW, he also reported that his father would threaten him sexually. Going into the forensic interview, Jordan anticipated Kaden might be reluctant to disclose the threats of sexual abuse because previous reports stated that Kaden couldn’t remember if any sexual abuse occurred.

title: "I can tell it was bleeding cause I like tasted blood" Ellie (9)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 9-year-old Ellie. Ellie disclosed to a school counselor that her mother hits her in her mouth and eye with an open hand. She stated the most recent incident happened the night before because she didn’t go to sleep. It was also reported by school officials that mother does not treat Ellie and her older brother the same. Mother punishes Ellie by not allowing her to participate in school activities, and does not provide Ellie with the same resources as her older brother. Going into the forensic interview, we thought Ellie might be reluctant to disclose because when she spoke to the CSW after her initial disclosure, she began to minimize the abuse.

title: “They keep on asking questions even though I tell them everything that’s the truth” Kaylee (11)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 11-year-old Kaylee. Kaylee disclosed that she was self-harming because her brother and mother argue a lot at home. She reported that her brother gets violent and punches holes in the wall. Kaylee also disclosed a previous suicide attempt, so going into the forensic interview, Jordan knew that she might have to conduct a suicide assessment. During the interview, Kaylee got very upset and combative with Jordan for having to be interviewed by so many professionals about the same allegations. So Jordan had to explain the reasons why she was asked to speak with Kaylee.

title: “My dad said it was not my dad, it was a person I was dreaming” Morgan (9)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Chrissy conducted in 2017 with 9-year-old Morgan. Morgan disclosed that her father would wake her up to do “sexy stuff.” She reported that he would touch her butt with his front part, and “white stuff” came out. Prior to the interview, it was discovered that the mother and father had reunited. When Chrissy interviewed Morgan, she recanted her allegations, stating that it was just a dream and that she had gotten caught watching a sexy movie.

title: The First Jane Doe in the Epstein case: S.G. (14)
summary: SG was the first child victim to be interviewed in the Palm Beach Epstein investigation. We will be reviewing the police interview with SG and her grand jury testimony. She initially denied everything, but gradually disclosed increasingly serious abuse.

title: "Stuck in the same cycle everyday" Ashley (14)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 14-year-old Ashley. Ashley disclosed that her stepfather began touching her under the guise of play wrestling. She reported multiple incidents of stepfather explicitly asking her to let him touch her. Prior to the interview, Ashley and her mother were AWOL from DCFS, so Jordan anticipated that Ashley might be reluctant to disclose the abuse.

title: “Everyone’s giving me different words for it” Claire (17)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 17-year-old Claire. Claire disclosed that her father had been forcing her to have sex with him for two years. She reported that it happens every other night while the rest of their family is sleeping. During Jordan’s interview with Claire, she explained that the details of the different incidents were the same, so Jordan had to use creative techniques to get at multiple episodes.

title: “All I ever feel is guilt, and it’s exhausting” Josie (15)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 15-year-old Josie. Josie disclosed that her stepfather had been sexually abusing her since she was four years old. When Josie was interviewed by the police and social workers, she reported having a hard time remembering details of the abuse because she tried to forget it. During my interview with Josie, she talked a lot about self-blame and being an active participant in the abuse, which led me to change my questioning techniques.

title: “Gave me the ick” Back to Basics: Ruth (11)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 11-year-old Ruth. Ruth disclosed that her stepfather was touching her inappropriately under the ruse of tickling. She also reported that he would take pictures of her in the shower. When Ruth was interviewed by her social worker, she denied these allegations, but then subsequently re-disclosed to the police. Going into the forensic interview, Jordan anticipated that she might be reluctant to disclose.

title: “With a stick and a shoe and a hanger” Skylar (7)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview that Jordan conducted with 7 year old Skylar. Skylar’s older sister, Callie (12), disclosed severe sexual abuse by her stepfather. Due to these allegations, Skylar was initially taken in for a forensic interview at another center and denied ever witnessing or experiencing sexual abuse by her father. A month later, she disclosed to her caregiver that her father had touched her everywhere, and he told her to keep quiet.

title: Back to Basics: Reviewing the Ten Step Interview Brynne (12)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview that I conducted with 12 year old Brynne. After her father tried to forcefully remove Brynne from school, she disclosed that he touched her and made her feel uncomfortable. She also reported feeling scared of her father because she witnessed him physically assault her adult sister. Brynne also said that her father would insist that she change her clothes out in the open. During my forensic interview with Brynne, she discusses the sexual intent behind the touch, saying, “if he did that, what if he thought about doing other things to me?”

title: “Like, no matter what, he’s my dad.” Bella (17)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 17 year old Bella. Bella disclosed that her tattoo artist sexually assaulted her. When asked why she did not tell her mother, Bella said it was because her own father was sexually assaulting her when she was 5 years old. She reported that she thought it was normal because he was her father. After her initial disclosure, Bella partially recanted the allegations by telling professionals that it was her cousin who sexually assaulted her.

title: “They want to catch if I’m lying or not” Caroline (14)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 14 year old Caroline. Caroline disclosed that after her stepfather came home drunk, he cornered her in the kitchen and sexually assaulted her. Stepfather told her that she is “beautiful and hot,” and she reported feeling uncomfortable and weird. After disclosing, she later recalled additional abuse.

title: “I don’t know” Bethany (5)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Jordan conducted with 5 year old Bethany. Bethany disclosed that her sister Victoria (9) touched her. When their mother found out, she physically assaulted Victoria, causing the police to be called to the home. When Bethany was forensically interviewed, she responded to most of Jordan's questions with "I don't know."

title: Disbelieving Witness Part II: Kayla (15) and Maria (16)
summary: In our last webinar, we reviewed an interview Cara conducted with 15 year old Kayla. Kayla disclosed that her Maternal Uncle/Adoptive Father has been sexually touching her inappropriately. She described abuse with force, including a specific incident in which she reported that her cousin Maria was in the room. When Maria was interviewed by Jordan, she denied ever witnessing her biological father abuse Kayla.

title: “He said, are you in love with me” Kayla (15)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 15 year old Kayla. She disclosed that her Maternal Uncle/Adoptive Father has been sexually touching her inappropriately. Kayla described forceful abuse and a specific incident where her Cousin Maria was in the room. When Maria was interviewed, she denied ever witnessing her biological father abuse Kayla.

title: “Stop. Just color.” Isabela (4)
summary: We will be examining an interview that Jordan conducted with 4 year old Isabela. Isabela disclosed that her uncle was hurting her with his “p” to a teacher at school. She continued to disclose when interviewed by other professionals, but due to her age she seems to struggle with consistency and memory.

title: “I wanted to be like taken away from my mom” Kira (10)
summary: This will be the second part in a two-part series where we examine the interviews of sisters Tammy (12) and Kira (10). Tammy disclosed that her Uncle would touch her and her sister Kira at night in bed from kindergarten to second grade. Kira disclosed that her mother told both sisters to say that nothing happened.

title: “All the times it was just the same” Tammy (12)
summary: This will be the first part in a two-part series where we examine the interviews of sisters Tammy (12) and Kira (10). Tammy disclosed that her Uncle would touch her and her sister Kira at night in bed from kindergarten to second grade. Kira disclosed mother telling the sisters to say that nothing happened.

title: Interviewing an Older Teen: “People say that these days, teenagers tend to lie to get out of anything”
summary: We will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 17 year old Ashley. When told that she was going to move in with her father, Ashley disclosed that father was physically and sexually abusive. She described abuse in which father would grab her and forcefully remove her clothing. Both her adult sibling and the police believed Ashley was fabricating the allegations because she did not want to live with father.

title: Sibling Witness Interview to Corroborate Abuse
summary: We will be reviewing a witness and screening interview that Jordan conducted with 7 year old Johana. Jordan interviewed Johana’s older sister Rut (11) about allegations of sexual abuse against her stepfather. In the interview, Rut described several instances where Johana could have witnessed the abuse. A few weeks later, Jordan interviewed Johana as a witness, and to screen for abuse. Even though Johana didn’t believe Rut, her forensic interview provided lots of useful information.

title: Novice Interviewer vs Reluctant Child
summary: We will be reviewing an interview that one of our former Forensic Interviewers conducted back in 2017. Madison (12) first disclosed sexual abuse from her father when re-enacting the abuse with her sister. She then reported experiencing repeated abuse.

title: Suicide and Self-Harm Disclosure During Forensic Interviews: How & When to Assess Risk & Safety Plan
summary: Jordan Sargent, MSW, will be joined by Lauren Maltby, PhD, to give a condensed version of their Suicide & Self-Harm Disclosure During Forensic Interviews: How & When to Assess Risk & Safety Plan talk they pre-recorded for the 40th Annual San Diego International Conference on Child and Family Maltreatment. The case review will focus on what to do, as a forensic interviewer, when a child mentions thoughts of suicidality and self-harm in a forensic interview. They will review current best practices on how to assess for safety. They will teach you how to positively pair open-ended invitations with the more traditionally closed-ended screening questions found in standardized screenings, like the ASQ. They will look at some real-world examples of evaluations during forensic interviews and will also discuss how to respond when a child exhibits a severe emotional reaction during an interview. Finally, they will discuss how to safety plan and go about further safety assessment post interview.

title: “If your dad was here, he could buy you anything” Ally (12)
summary: Tomorrow, we will be reviewing an interview I conducted with 12-year-old Ally. Ally disclosed to a doctor that someone in her home was touching her, but wouldn’t say who. When interviewed by social workers, she disclosed that it was her stepfather. The next day Ally told her mother that she made it all up.

title: When the Defense Investigator Leads the Child
summary: Tomorrow, we will be looking at a homicide case with a child witness. 9-year-old Kylie witnessed her mother get into a physical altercation with a homeless man who was trying to enter their vehicle. Kylie's mother then hit the victim with her car and fled the scene. After her mother was arrested, Kylie underwent both a Forensic Interview and a Defense Investigative Interview by the mother’s Defense Attorney

title: “It felt like it wasn’t an accident”
summary: Tomorrow, we will be looking at Gabrielle’s 3rd interview. Gabrielle conducted with 13 year old Charlotte. Prior to a visitation with their father, Charlotte and her brother Diego told their mother that their father was touching them inappropriately. When interviewed by Law Enforcement, Charlotte asked the officer to tell her father to stop touching them on their private parts.

title: “I’m Scared”: Kali (10) What to do when the child wants to stop
summary: Tomorrow, we will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted with 10 year old Kali. Kali disclosed sexual abuse to the police twice, first in Nevada, and then months later in Los Angeles. Kali said that mother started sexually abusing her when she was 5 years old. In Jordan's interview, Kali was extremely reluctant to disclose both general and specific details about the abuse. They had to take multiple breaks since Kali would begin to emotionally shut down when addressing specific topics, like body parts and specific acts.

title: “Okay, Porky” Interviewing the Sassy Teen
summary: Tomorrow, we will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted with 14 year old Katelynn. Katelynn’s mother called the police on Katelynn during a family altercation. During the interview with LE, Katelynn disclosed that she was sexually abused by her father when she was 5 years old. Katelynn has a history of suicidality, substance use, and running away.

title: “We never did like him” Back to Basics Interviewing Refresher
summary: Tomorrow, we will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted with 11 year old Isabella back in 2019. Isabella reported to a school counselor that her father had been sexually abusing her from ages 4-9. Her stepfather was arrested and later convicted of 288.5(a) Continuous Sexual Abuse of Child.

title: Conflicting Sibling Testimony
summary: Tomorrow will be the second of a two-part webinar where we look at Cara’s Forensic Interviews of siblings Aliyah (10) and Malachi (9). Aliyah reported that her mother had multiple personalities, and her alternate personality, Phoenix, would often lie on top of her in an ambiguous way. We will review Malachi’s interview as a potential witness.

title: Double Recantation
summary: We will review a case where Jordan interviewed 2 sisters who alleged abuse against their stepfather. Keyla (13) alleged repeated abuse in 2 separate police interviews. Keyla later began to recant, and denied her first two Forensic Interviews. Isabella (9) spontaneously reported feeling uncomfortable when stepfather was tickling her, but later said the incident was only a prank. Isabella was very forthcoming about events in the family that helped explain Keyla’s recantation.

title: Gabby’s First Interview
summary: We will be reviewing Gabrielle’s first interview! Gabrielle interviewed 13-year-old Hadasha who disclosed physical abuse from her mother and sexual abuse from mother’s boyfriend. Hadasha had previously disclosed abuse from mother’s boyfriend in 2023, but the investigations were unfounded after Hadasha recanted.

title: Jorge (11)
summary: We will be reviewing an anonymized interview conducted by another center. We will be looking at an interview with Jorge, an 11-year old trans boy who alleged abuse from his mother’s boyfriend. His initial disclosure described somewhat moderate abuse, however in his interview he discloses repeated rape.

title: Brother-Brother Abuse: Body Cam VS Forensic Interview
summary: We will be continuing a 2-part series in which we review a complicated case involving 4 brothers. We will be looking at the youngest brother, Jante (12)’s forensic interview and police interview. Jante was the first brother to initially disclose, however he minimized the abuse in his forensic interview.

title: Teen Disclosure of Brother-Brother Abuse
summary: Tomorrow will be the first part of a 2-part series in which we review a complicated case involving 4 brothers. We’ll start by looking at Jordan’s interview with 14-year old Jamari. His brother had reported witnessing Jamari being sexually abused by 17 year old brother, however Jamari denied this when interviewed by social workers and law enforcement. In Jordan’s interview, Jamari disclosed abuse for the first time and shared some feelings of embarrassment and reluctance.

title: Reluctance and Non-Response: When to Conduct a Follow-Up Interview
summary: We will be reviewing two interviews that Jordan and I conducted with 11-year-old Adalyn who disclosed severe abuse from her paternal grandfather. Adalyn was extremely reluctant and was unable to even speak in her first interview. She agreed to return for a second interview with Jordan in which she was able to disclose some parts of the abuse, before shutting down again.

title: Recantation Case Study
summary: We will be reviewing an early interview that Tom conducted with nine-year-old Nasha. Nasha initially disclosed both sexual abuse from her mother’s boyfriend, and that her grandmother had let men rape Nasha in exchange for money. The grandmother was arrested and charged for these acts. However, Nasha recanted the grandmother’s abuse shortly after testifying at the preliminary hearing. The DA then invited Tom to interview Nasha.

title: Minimal Facts: Conflicts between Police and Forensic Interviewing
summary: We will be reviewing the body cam footage for an interview Jordan conducted last September with 8 year old Alondra. We will be highlighting how challenges in police interviews can be avoided with more comprehensive minimal facts training for Law Enforcement.

title: Child Witness to Homicide Matthew (6): My dad is the best dad in the world
summary: We will be reviewing an interview that Tom conducted in 2004 with six-year-old Matthew, the only eyewitness to his mother’s murder. Matthew recanted at trial, but the interview was admitted into evidence.

title: “I Don’t Want to Explain It”
summary: We will be reviewing a webinar that Jordan conducted with 10-year-old Valerie back in 2019. Valerie disclosed that her father raped her on two instances in the same day.

title: Tactics for Long Interviews
summary: Tomorrow we will be examining a 3 hour interview I recently conducted with Isabel (14). Following an altercation between her mother and her step-father’s family, Isabel disclosed that her step-father had been sexually abusing her when mother wasn’t home. During our interview Isabel was incredibly talkative, and her first narrative lasted over 30 minutes.

title: Consolidating Information Body Cam Interviews of Mother, Child, and Suspect
summary: Tomorrow we will be examining a case that was handled by another CAC. We will review the child’s forensic interview as well as body cam footage from the police interview of the child, the mother, and the alleged abuser. RR is a 6-year-old child that alleged that her mother’s boyfriend was touching her inappropriately on multiple incidents.

title: Minimization and Miscommunication
summary: We will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted for a case in which Alondra (8) alleged repeated abuse by her two older brothers, Isaac (14) and Josue (16).

title: “Why is there a lotta . . . bad stuff happening in our house?” Bodycams on Esther (6), Ana (9), and Bryan (11)
summary: We will be continuing our discussion on a case in which Jordan interviewed 3 siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator. First, we looked at Ana (9) and Esther’s (6) forensic interviews to review developmental differences in the recollection and narrative of the same event. Last webinar, we examined Bryan’s (11) forensic interview to discuss delayed disclosure and reluctance.

title: Reluctance or Recall?
summary: We will be continuing our discussion on a case in which Jordan interviewed 3 siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator. Last webinar we looked at Ana (9) and Esther’s (6) interviews to review developmental differences in the recollection and narrative of the same event.

title: Interviewing by Age
summary: We will be discussing a case in which Jordan interviewed 3 siblings who alleged abuse from the same perpetrator. We will start by looking at the interviews of the younger two siblings who both disclosed joint abuse. 9-year-old Ana reported to a teacher that her adult brother, Augustin, tried to put his penis in her and her sister’s mouth.

title: Minimal Facts Interviewing: Expert Panel Discussion
summary: In this webinar, we’ll be joined by an expert panel who will discuss the pros and cons of minimal facts interviews by first responders. We’ll discuss what a minimal facts interview is, when it is warranted (and when immediate referral to a CAC is preferable), and what factors to consider. We’ll also discuss good questions for minimal facts interviews.

title: Body Cam vs Forensic Interview
summary: We’ll discuss a 13 year old child’s disclosure of repeated abuse by her stepfather, starting with examination of the body cam footage of the first responders. We’ll discuss how minimal facts interviewing could improve the investigative process, and reduce the number of inconsistencies and uncertainties in children’s reports. We’ll also discuss steps forensic interviewers might take to address those inconsistencies when questioning children.

title: Clarifying Sexual Touch (Part 2)
summary: We will be building off last week’s discussion on clarifying touch. We will be reviewing effective strategies for eliciting details regarding sexual touch and penetration. We’ll present examples of where questioning went well, and no so well, including our own experiences. We will look at examples using diagrams, tissue boxes, and very direct questions. We will also discuss ideas on how to work with extremely reluctant children when all other strategies fail.

title: Clarifying Sexual Touch (Part 1)
summary: We will be reviewing effective strategies for eliciting details regarding sexual touch and penetration. We’ll say a little about the legal standards (but of course you’ll want to talk further with your DA). We’ll review the limited research examining how best to ask questions. We’ll present examples of where questioning went well, and no so well, including our own experiences. We’re interested in hearing from you about your approach, and getting your thoughts regarding the “tissue box test.”  This will give everyone insight into what approaches to try (and what approaches should be researched further).

title: "Cocomelon says that" Danely (5)
summary: Tomorrow we will be reviewing an interview that Jordan conducted with 5 year old Danely. Danely disclosed abuse by her older brother Ethan, who is diagnosed with autism. She reported that Ethan asked both Danely and her cousin to play hospital and take off their pants. He then touched the girls in their privates. During her interview with Jordan, Danely was very energetic and distractible. Join us tomorrow as we review Jordan’s interview, and effective strategies for young children who are chatty, but reluctant.

title: Araceli (13): What do you mean?
summary: Tomorrow we will be joined by a special guest and fellow Forensic Interviewer, Crystal Thorne. Crystal has been an avid attendee of the webinars and uses the Ten-Step in her interviewing practices. We will be peer-reviewing an interview that Crystal conducted with a shy and reluctant 12-year-old girl who disclosed sexual abuse by her paternal grandfather. Join us as we discuss Crystal’s methods, tactics for overcoming reluctance, and review the NICHD recommended supportive statements.

title: "I'm pretty sure you know what that is" AJ (13)
summary: We will be reviewing an interview Cara conducted with 13-year-old AJ. AJ is a trans boy with he/him pronouns who is severely suicidal. AJ gave a note to his adult sister disclosing long term repeated rape and sodomy by their stepfather. His sister then filed a report with the police. Join us tomorrow to review the case and the interview. We will be reflecting on a previous interview I had conducted with a trans boy and comparing the two cases. We will discuss risk factors trans youth face and how we incorporate suicide assessments into our practice.

title: Peer Review Recommendations (Lisbet, 10)
summary: We will be debuting our long-awaited Peer Review Template in Google Sheets. We will teach you all how to access the template as well as all tips and tricks for using it. We will walk you through the peer-review process including Question Type coding with an interview conducted at our center in 2007.

title: "It was really tight that my hand couldn't breathe" Desiree (10)
summary: We will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted with 10-year-old Desiree. Spurred by an allegation of inappropriate touch from maternal aunt, Desiree's mother asked her two daughters if stepfather Alberto had been touching them inappropriately. Desiree confirmed that Alberto had touched her inappropriately, and later reported sodomy and vaginal touch to law enforcement and social workers. Join us tomorrow as we review Jordan's interviewing strategies. We will examine the most effective language used by Jordan and explore which tactics helped Desiree overcome her reluctance.

title: "I get mad at my brain and sometimes I hate it" Lorenzo
summary: We will be looking at an interview that Jordan conducted recently with 7-year-old Lorenzo regarding two perpetrators, his stepfather and a friend his age. Lorenzo first reported sexual abuse by his stepfather when he was 4 years old and participated in a forensic interview regarding the allegation. DCFS found that the count was sustained, and the child was removed from contact with his stepfather. In 2022, DCFS was informed that the child now states that the perpetrator was not the stepfather, but a friend the child's age. It was from this new allegation that Jordan conducted a forensic interview with Lorenzo. Join us tomorrow as we discuss the case, both interviews, and the challenges of interviewing young children.

title: "Right here it will be black all the time" Ellie (13)
summary: For our first interview of the year, we will be returning back to the basics and focusing on the structure and assets of the 10-Step. We will be looking at an interview Cara conducted in December with 13-year-old Ellie. Ellie had disclosed being touched by her father repeatedly over a 2-month period. Ellie was pretty reluctant in our interview, so we will take a closer look at what supportive statements helped Ellie overcome her reluctance. We will also discuss different strategies Cara could have used to elicit more detailed responses.

title: "Right here it will be black all the time" Chantal (12)
summary: We're going to look at an interview from 2016 conducted by one of our past interviewers, Catherine Liang. We will be discussing 12-year-old Chantal's interview, who had previously reported severe sexual abuse from her father. During her interview, Chantal partially recanted and greatly minimized the abuse. We will analyze Catherine's approach for a partial recantation, and discuss her successes and areas for improvement.

title: Alondra (5): Is it Abuse? "Because he never brings all my Barbies"
summary: This webinar examines an interview conducted with 5-year-old Alondra, who disclosed that her father touched her private part while bathing her during a custody visit. The case raises difficult questions about distinguishing routine caretaking from sexual abuse, particularly given Alondra's age, her father's unfamiliarity with bathing her, and her history of vulvovaginitis. The discussion explores how question type affects the quality of information obtained from young children, the challenges of interpreting ambiguous disclosures, and how prior allegations within the same family can both increase suspicion and complicate interpretation. Join us as we review this interview and the broader challenge of differentiating abuse from caretaking in bath-time cases.

title: Justin (9): I haven't really been feeling like myself
summary: We will be looking at a recent interview Cara conducted with 9-year-old Justin who was abused by his father. We will discuss Justin's reluctance, and his resistance to our allegation questions. We will look at the ways that the 10-Step helped Justin overcome his reluctance and eventually disclose new information, including a second incident of abuse. We will also discuss what tactics can help reduce a child’s anxiety and emotional arousal.

title: Dayana (8) What percent are you in? If you get to 100, are you done?
summary: We are building off of our webinar from last week to continue our discussion of assent with Child Psychologist and Forensic Interviewer, Lauren Maltby. We will be taking a closer look at Jordan's two interviews with 8-year-old Dayana. As we saw in last week's Webinar, Dayana was extremely reluctant and had an intense emotional reaction to disclosure questions. We will look at the way that Jordan was able to use assent to negotiate Dayana's return for a second interview, and eventual disclosure. We will also discuss the ways that the 10-Step and Jordan’s practices helped Dayana overcome her extreme reluctance.

title: Are children capable of informed consent?
summary: We will be joined by a special guest, child psychologist and forensic interviewer Lauren Maltby of Harbor UCLA, to discuss the process of obtaining assent from a child before an interview. Using the transcript of an assent conversation Lauren had with a teen, we will analyze the way an interviewer can obtain assent, and discuss the benefits and concerns of incorporating assent into common practice. We also look at an interview Jordan conducted with an extremely reluctant child, and examine the way that obtaining assent helped Jordan negotiate disclosure.

title: Emely (11) Revisited: I just wanted to creep into a little ball
summary: This week we reviewed our first ever webinar, Emely (11 years old) and examined the ways that the 10-Step has changed over the years both formally and informally. We review the work of a previous interviewer, Chrissy Del Pozzo, and highlight the changes we’ve made in our interviewing practices over the last 5 years.

title: And I was like, yes I know what my body parts are. Clay (12)
summary: We will be discussing Cara’s first interview, a case with a 12-year-old trans boy. We will review successes, areas for improvement, and my interviewing strategies. We will also go over the child's discussion of his previous disclosures and risk factors for reluctance. We will analyze the general interviewing strategy according to the 10-Step and the importance of each tactic.

title: Mikayla (14)
summary: This case review discussed an interview Jordan conducted with a 14-year-old girl who had been kidnapped and then sexually abused, along with her friend. We'll be reviewing my interview and additionally discussing the inconsistencies of the minor's disclosures to law enforcement and children services. Issues discussed will include how the perceived inconsistencies by law enforcement and children's services affected the case, how to ask about inconsistencies in a supportive manner, and how to question teenagers about sensitive topics without implying they are at fault.

title: Dylan (13)
summary: Dylan (13) was interviewed by Owen based on allegations of abuse made by his sister despite never disclosing himself. Dr. Lyon and team discuss preparing for an interview with limited information available, overcoming reluctance to disclose, and providing neutral support during a forensic interview. We additionally review the supportive statements suggested in the Revised NICHD Protocol as well as sharing some supportive techniques we often use in our interviews.

title: How much little girls and young women know about their genitalia, and how little the law understands
summary: The USC Center for the Changing Family and the Child Interviewing Lab hosted a virtual panel event on the difficulties in questioning girls and young women about their genitalia in cases of sexual abuse and rape. Dr Thomas Lyon (USC Gould School of Law) discussed the legal requirements for establishing the nature and invasiveness of genital touch. Next, Shalon Nienow, M.D. (Rady Children’s Hospital, San Diego) described the process of forensic pediatric genital examinations and shared her experience of assessing children’s and adolescent's knowledge of genital anatomy. Dr Zsofia Szojka (USC Gould School of Law) concluded by presenting preliminary findings revealing difficulties in attorneys' questioning of children in sexual abuse and rape trials.

title: Force
summary: Dr. Lyon, Jordan, and Owen discuss establishing the use of force in child abuse cases. First, we review the legal requirements for force, and discuss some legal cases describing what is sufficient. Then we examine how children describe force and resistance, and what kinds of questions elicit this information, looking at excerpts from our interviews. Finally, we discuss some dangers in asking children yes/no questions about force and resistance.

title: "I could just imagine the pain my mom is going through" Jacqueline R. (10)
summary: Jacqueline (10) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent in 2018. Dr. Lyon, Jordan, and Owen review the interview four years after it was conducted and provide suggestions as to how the interview could be improved. Issues discussed include script vs. episodic recall, the “pseudotemporal” problem, and providing support while remaining objective. In addition, we discuss strategies for peer reviewing past interviews and how to continuously improve as an interviewer.

title: 4-to 15-year-olds' difficulties in interpreting invitations asking "about the time"
summary: Dr. Lyon and staff members present and discuss several research projects from the lab, see below for brief summaries of each paper: Owen Friend: This paper explored children's difficulties interpreting invitations containing temporal language in forensic interviews, providing suggestions for interviewers to ask developmentally appropriate questions when seeking narrative information about specific "times" abuse occurred (e.g. first time, last time, worst time, etc.). Hannah Siepmann: This paper examines how adolescent victims of commercial sexual exploitation are perceived by juries when they exhibit reluctance in court and whether their race affects this perception. Dr. Zsofia Szojka: This paper investigated children’s sensitivity to the implied Wh- question in yes/no questions with the polarity terms ‘some’ and ‘any’ and whether negative polarity questions lead to a ‘no bias’. Aga Nogalska: This paper examined how adolescent victims of child sex abuse express reluctance during forensic interviews. It explored how reluctance reduces the amount of information available about the abuse, and how prior disclosure of abuse influences reluctance during the forensic interview.

title: Truth-Lie Competency (& the Ten Step)
summary: Dr. Lyon and team discuss issues regarding children’s competency to testify including literature on children’s understanding of the truth and lies, legal requirements for children to be deemed competent to testify, and when/how to conduct a competency assessment. Additionally, Dr. Lyon and team discuss interviewing protocol used for training in Washington state and compare Washington’s protocols to the Ten Step 3.0

title: And she was just laughing and telling me basically, you're high it's not true. 14-year-old Lenay (Part 2)
summary: Lenay (14) recanted sexual abuse allegations she’d made against her stepfather, but had her original allegation to police captured via body-worn camera. In a follow-up to the previous case review, Dr. Lyon and Jordan discuss issues regarding police interviews recorded on body-worn cameras and the pros and cons of recording interviews with child victims.

title: And she was just laughing and telling me basically, you're high it's not true. 14-year-old Lenay
summary: Lenay (14) was interviewed by Owen Friend and recanted sexual abuse allegations she’d made against her stepfather. Dr. Lyon and Owen discuss preparing for an interview when expecting a recantation, supportive strategies for reluctant children, and issues regarding police interviews recorded on body-worn cameras.

title: "Are we done yet? Are we almost done? Are we done yet? [Yodels into juice box]" 7-year old Nala
summary: Nala (7) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent. Dr. Lyon and Jordan review the interview three years after it was conducted and provide suggestions as to how the interview could be improved. Issues discussed include maintaining the attention of a distracted child, using support to overcome reluctance, and distinguishing between episodic and script recall.

title: "Sometimes I kinda wish that I didn't anything at all" 14-year-old Sayuri
summary: S (14) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent. Dr. Lyon and team discuss repeated interviews for children who are initially unwilling to disclose including improvised interview structure for particularly reluctant children, supportive strategies, script vs. episodic invitations, and ambivalence towards promising to tell the truth.

title: Recommendations for improving recantation interviews Sofia (12), Isabella (13) and Emma (10) "it's the truth that I'm lying"
summary: Dr. Lyon and team review recantations from other Child Advocacy Centers and provide peer review, discussing interview protocol for children that recant. Issues discussed include how to structure a recant interview, how to ask children about prior disclosures, and how to provide support for recanters.

title: 11-year-old Valerie: but my dad never touched me in my life, never ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever ever never
summary: V (11) was interviewed by Owen Friend. Dr. Lyon and team discuss dealing with spontaneous disclosure during rapport building, regaining a child’s aenon who has lost focus, providing support and clarification for reluctant children, and differences in screening for sexual and physical abuse

title: 6-year-old Brittany: "Kids can't really know this"
summary: B (6) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent. Dr. Lyon and team discuss how to implement the 10-step with younger children, issue with interviewing younger children remotely, and how to use NEXT and MORE invitations to elicit a complete narrative.

title: The (Annotated) Ten Step Interview (Version 3)
summary: Dr. Tom Lyon and team continue discussing updated and changes to the 10-Step forensic interviewing protocol and take a look at the in depth annotated version of the protocol.

title: The Ten Step Investigative Interview (Version 3)
summary: Dr. Tom Lyon and team discuss updates and changes to the 10-Step forensic interviewing protocol.

title: Productive Wh- Questions: Felt, Seen, Heard, Said, Hands and Mouth
summary: We discuss supplemental wh- questions that we've found to be especially effective, including references to what was seen, heard, said, and done with the hands and mouth. We give examples from our interviews and discuss why these questions may elicit information that invitations do not. In addition, we discuss both experimental and field studies that examine the effectiveness of these questions.

title: 12-year-old Andrea: "I ruined everything and I just want everything to go back to normal"
summary: A (12) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent. We review a case involving a 12-year-old female who recanted her allegations and discuss different techniques to use in order to still have a productive interview. In addition, we go over some common risk factors that increase the likelihood of recantation and look at some statistics from our sample of recanters that we have collected over the years.

title: Note-Taking During Forensic Interviews
summary: This webinar is all about note-taking during the forensic interview. Georgia Lundon discusses the research surrounding the perceived risks and benefits of note-taking, and suggests that the benefits far outweigh the potential costs. This webinar features a practice element and a Q and A from attendees. The Powerpoint slides (with links to mentioned research) can be found in the shared Google Drive folder.

title: "It was like if someone put like a big food in my mouth and I couldn't fit it." (7-year-old Christopher)
summary: C (7 years) was interviewed by Jordan Sargent. We discuss how to overcome young grade school children's difficulties in providing a narrative through WH- questions that enable them to proceed step by step.

title: "But then I heard the story, what happened to Serenity" (8-year-old Savannah)
summary: This case review follows on from the last. We discuss how younger sister S (8 years) was eager to help her sister’s story, and how her eagerness to help her sister could be challenged by the defense later on. We discuss the best way to encourage children to report on what they saw, rather than what they have heard from others.

title: "And in my child mind I didn't know anything that it was bad" (13-year-old Serenity & 8-year-old Savannah)
summary: Sisters (8 and 13 years) were interviewed by Jordan Sargent. We discuss how bribes might have caused one of the sisters to be more reluctant to disclose abuse and to experience feelings of self-blame. We go on to discuss how some "milder" forms of abuse may be more traumatic for some children.

title: "My mom is going to choose him over all of us" (14-year-old Tiara & 10-year-old Scarlet) (Part 2)
summary: Sisters (female, 10 and 14 years) were interviewed by Jordan Sargent. We discuss the early stages of abuse and the different reactions by both girls. We also discuss sibling dynamics and supportiveness, corroboration, recantation, maternal supportiveness, familial pressures, and the impact of disclosure on mental health. This webinar is highly recommended.

title: "My mom is going to choose him over all of us" (14-year-old Tiara & 10-year-old Scarlet)
summary: We ran into technical issues early on in this webinar, but hosted a Q and A session with many interesting questions from attendees.

title: Esperanza (14 years old)
summary: E (female, 14 years) was interviewed by Hailey Konovalov. This child immediately disclosed the abuse and we discuss why and how this may have occurred and compare this to delayed disclosures. This interview addresses abuse dynamics, as well as how the trauma of the abuse impacts the child. This webinar is particularly helpful for interviewers struggling with how to follow-up on a long and productive initial narrative.

title: Recantation: Azul (13)
summary: This webinar focuses on a teenager who disclosed abuse to friends through social media before later recanting. The discussion highlights best practices for interviewing youth who have made multiple disclosures, documenting prior reports, and understanding how family reactions may influence a child’s willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Bryanna (13)
summary: This training-focused webinar examines forensic interviewing methods and the relationship between question types and the amount of information children provide. Using a real interview as an example, the presenters analyze open-ended questioning, narrative development, and techniques that encourage detailed and reliable responses.

title: Question Type and Productivity: Delilah (11) and Bryanna (13)
summary: This webinar explores how different interviewing approaches affect the quantity and quality of information obtained from children. Through case examples, the presenters discuss the impact of open-ended prompts, potential investigator bias, and strategies for obtaining detailed narratives while maintaining a neutral interviewing stance.

title: Case Review: 14 year old Deavyn
summary: This webinar examines one of the lab’s early remote forensic interviews and discusses the benefits and challenges of conducting child interviews through video technology. The presenters review interviewing techniques, rapport building in virtual settings, and considerations for maintaining interview quality when in-person interviews are not possible.

title: Case Review: 12 year old Lesly
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving repeated allegations of abuse and explores how caregiver responses can influence disclosure patterns. The discussion focuses on family support, disbelief, blame, and the role these factors play in children’s willingness to maintain or withdraw allegations over time.

title: Case Review: 13 year old Renee
summary: This webinar examines a case involving a 13-year-old who later recanted previous allegations of sexual abuse. The discussion focuses on common reasons children recant, how family dynamics and concerns about disrupting relationships can influence disclosures, and effective interviewing strategies for exploring prior statements without pressuring the child. Viewers will learn how forensic interviewers evaluate competing explanations for disclosure and recantation.

title: Case Review: 11 year old Matthew
summary: This webinar examines a case involving an 11-year-old boy who disclosed repeated sexual abuse. The presenters discuss unique challenges that may arise when interviewing male victims, including embarrassment, shame, reluctance to discuss abuse, and strategies for helping children provide detailed narratives in a supportive environment.

title: Case Review: 9 year old Faith
summary: This webinar reviews a case involving allegations of problematic sexual behavior between siblings and explores the challenges of interviewing children when caregivers disagree about what occurred. The presenters discuss credibility assessment, family responses to disclosures, and factors that may increase the likelihood of recantation or inconsistent reporting.
